Merge the dormant accounts into a single shared contractor account for simplicity, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
Disable the accounts immediately, verify with owners whether any are still needed, then delete per retention policy
explain: Dormant accounts are live attack surface, so disable first, then validate any claimed need before deletion. Random passwords on enabled accounts and merged shared accounts keep the exposure.

q: An executive's assistant routinely logs in with the executive's credentials to manage email. Which principle does this violate, and what is the fix?
options: Accountability: credentials must never be shared; delegate mailbox permissions to the assistant's own account instead
Availability: the executive should keep a second account so both can log in at once, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
Confidentiality: the assistant should use a VPN whenever signing in as the executive, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
Integrity: the executive's password should be longer so delegated use is safer, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
explain: Shared credentials destroy attribution of actions; mailbox delegation achieves the business need under the assistant's own identity. The issue is not solved by VPNs, longer passwords, or duplicate accounts.

q: During an audit, several employees are found to have both the ability to create vendors and to approve payments to them. This is PRIMARILY a failure of what?
options: Least privilege, because both functions are administrative in nature, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
Separation of duties, because one person can both set up a payee and pay them, enabling fraud
Password policy, because the two functions should use different passwords, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
Access recertification, because the entitlements were granted more than a year ago, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
explain: Creating a vendor and paying that vendor are conflicting duties that must be split between people. Least privilege is related, but the specific defect is the toxic combination in one person's hands.

q: A firm is tightening authentication for remote access. Which option is the COMPLETE correct configuration?
options: Require authenticator-app MFA for all users and extend VPN session timeouts to reduce repeated prompts, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
Require passkeys for remote access and allow SMS codes as an unrestricted fallback for every user, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
Require passkeys or authenticator-app MFA, evaluate device health and sign-in risk with conditional access, and screen credentials against breach data
Evaluate device health with conditional access and require password changes every 60 days for remote users, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
explain: Strong factors, risk-based conditional access, and breach screening address different attack paths and belong together; each distractor weakens one leg with long sessions, unrestricted SMS fallback, or password rotation alone.

q: A help desk technician is socially engineered into resetting MFA for an attacker posing as an employee. Which control MOST reduces recurrence?
options: Log all MFA resets and review the log during the quarterly access review, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
Shorten the validity window of TOTP codes from 30 seconds to 15 seconds, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
Allow MFA resets only during business hours on weekdays, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
Require in-person or video-verified identity proofing plus manager approval before any MFA reset is performed
explain: Resets are the weak point attackers exploit, so strong identity proofing at reset time is the preventive control. Logging and reviews are detective, and code windows and hours do not verify identity.

q: Which statement BEST describes how backup codes should be handled?
options: They are single-use recovery codes generated at enrollment, stored securely by the user, and invalidated after use
They are permanent secondary passwords that can be reused whenever the phone is unavailable, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
They are held by the help desk and read aloud to users who call in to request them, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
They are emailed to the user each time a recovery is needed so nothing must be stored, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
explain: Backup codes are generated once, kept by the user, and each works a single time. Help-desk-held or emailed codes turn recovery into a social-engineering or inbox-compromise path.

q: A cloud tenant shows an external consultant was given the Owner role 'temporarily' eight months ago and still has it. Which two practices would have prevented this?
options: Annual password rotation for cloud accounts and a naming convention for consultant accounts, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
Just-in-time grants with automatic expiry, backed by periodic access reviews that flag stale entitlements
Requiring the consultant to sign an NDA and complete security awareness training, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
Documenting temporary grants in the change calendar and reviewing changes monthly, following the standard change process used across the organization
explain: Time-boxed grants expire on their own, and reviews catch whatever slips through. NDAs, naming conventions, and calendar notes do not remove standing privilege.

q: An attacker registers a domain that looks like the company portal and emails staff a link. Staff with password plus SMS MFA are compromised; staff with passkeys are not. Why?
options: Passkey users received a different email because the attacker targeted only SMS users, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
The lookalike domain could not obtain an HTTPS certificate, so passkey browsers blocked it, following the standard change process used across the organization
The passkey would not be released for the lookalike origin, while passwords and SMS codes can be typed or relayed into the fake page
SMS codes expire in 30 seconds, which was too short for the attacker to relay them, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
explain: Real-time phishing proxies relay passwords and codes, but origin-bound passkeys simply refuse to authenticate to the wrong site. Attackers can obtain valid certificates for lookalike domains.

q: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a privileged access management (PAM) solution?
options: To provide single sign-on for all business applications used by general staff, following the standard change process used across the organization
To replace the identity provider as the authoritative source for user accounts, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
To scan endpoints for malware using administrator-level system permissions, under the direction of the accountable system owner
To vault, check out, rotate, and record the use of privileged credentials so admin access is controlled and accountable
explain: PAM governs the privileged layer: credential vaulting, controlled checkout, rotation, and session recording. SSO, identity sourcing, and endpoint scanning are separate functions.

q: A biometric door reader is tuned so legitimate staff are frequently rejected, and staff begin propping the door open. What does this illustrate?
options: Excessive false rejection undermines the control itself, driving workarounds that remove protection entirely
Biometrics are unsuitable for physical access and should always be replaced with badges, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
The reader's false acceptance rate is too high, allowing unauthorized entry, under the direction of the accountable system owner
Staff require disciplinary action, which is the primary fix for control failures, using only the tools already approved for this environment
explain: When a control rejects legitimate users too often, people bypass it — here by propping the door, which is worse than the original setting. The problem described is false rejection, not false acceptance.

q: An organization wants departing employees' access removed even when HR notification is delayed. Which design helps MOST?
options: Ask managers to email IT whenever a team member resigns or is terminated, under the direction of the accountable system owner, using only the tools already approved for this environment
Automate deprovisioning from the HR system of record so a termination status change triggers disablement without manual tickets
Run a monthly report of accounts that have not logged in for 30 days, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
Require employees to surrender their badge at the exit interview, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
explain: HR-driven automation removes the human delay between the employment decision and account disablement. Manager emails, inactivity reports, and badge collection are slower or incomplete.

q: Which option lists the COMPLETE correct joiner provisioning for a new financial analyst?
options: Create the account by copying the previous analyst's account, enable MFA, and grant the finance application group, using only the tools already approved for this environment
Create the account from the analyst role template, grant local admin on the workstation, and enable MFA enrollment, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
Create the account from the analyst role template, enable MFA enrollment at first login, grant the finance application group, and schedule the first access review
Create the account manually, grant the finance application group, and add the all-employees distribution list as the only entitlement, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
explain: Role-template provisioning with MFA and scheduled review is the complete, controlled path. Copying a predecessor imports creep, local admin is unrelated excess privilege, and the manual option omits MFA and review.

q: A user can view payroll data because her role was merged with another department's role during a system migration and never split again. This is an example of what?
options: A federation failure between the payroll system and the identity provider, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
An example of just-in-time access granting rights outside its time window, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
A break-glass activation that was not reviewed after the migration, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
Privilege creep through role accumulation, where entitlements pile up without removal
explain: Roles merging and never being pruned is classic privilege creep: access accumulates and old rights are never taken away. No emergency access or federation issue is described.

q: Which control BEST ensures an administrator cannot quietly use a vaulted credential without anyone knowing?
options: Session recording with real-time alerting on checkout of sensitive credentials in the PAM system
Requiring administrators to write the checkout reason in a shared team log, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
Rotating vaulted passwords every 90 days instead of after each use, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
Restricting the PAM vault to business hours so nights are uncovered, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
explain: Recording plus alerting makes privileged use visible as it happens; self-written logs can be falsified, and rotation schedules do not observe the session itself.

q: A SOAR playbook automatically isolates any host whose EDR risk score crosses a threshold. One morning it isolates the CEO's laptop during a board meeting based on a faulty sensor reading. What does this illustrate?
options: SOAR platforms should never be connected to EDR tools because the integration is inherently unsafe, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
Automation executes the wrong action at machine speed when its trigger is wrong, so scope, testing, and guardrails must be designed in
Risk scores should be removed from playbooks and replaced with manual analyst review of every alert, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
The EDR vendor is solely responsible because the playbook only followed the score it was given, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
explain: Every automation has a risk twin: a bad input produces a bad action everywhere, fast. The fix is guardrails and tested scope, not abandoning the integration.

q: An agentic AI system in the SOC can isolate hosts and open cases on its own, but blocking a sender domain across the whole tenant requires analyst approval. Why is the second action gated?
options: AI agents are technically unable to change mail flow rules, so a human must perform the clicks, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
Blocking actions are always handled by chatbots rather than agents in a SOAR design, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
Tenant-wide blocking is high-impact and hard to reverse, so it sits above the agent's autonomous authority and needs a human gate
The approval step exists only to satisfy auditors and has no operational purpose, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
explain: Agentic AI authority is tiered: pre-approved reversible actions run alone, while broad or irreversible actions require human approval. The gate is an operational guardrail, not a technical limitation.

q: A SOC deploys a chatbot to handle tier-1 work. Which use BEST matches its intended role?
options: Deciding whether to notify regulators about a confirmed breach of customer data, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
Approving firewall rule changes requested by application teams during incidents, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
Negotiating directly with a ransomware group on behalf of the organization, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
Answering routine questions, summarizing tickets, and drafting first-pass analysis so analysts start ahead
explain: Chatbots absorb routine volume — summaries, drafts, common answers — while consequential decisions such as notification, approvals, and negotiation stay with accountable humans.

q: Instead of alerting on a fixed threshold of failed logins, a system learns each user's normal sign-in pattern and flags a 3 a.m. bulk download by an account that never downloads files. This is an example of what?
options: An AI-augmented baseline that flags deviation from learned normal behavior rather than a static rule
A signature-based detection that matched the download against a known malware hash, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
Predictive analysis forecasting which accounts will be targeted next quarter, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
A guardrail preventing an automation from acting outside its approved scope, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
explain: The system learned what normal looks like per user and flagged the deviation, which is the definition of an AI-augmented baseline. No forecast, signature match, or automation boundary is described.

q: A security model forecasts that unpatched VPN appliances are likely to be exploited in the next two weeks based on threat trends, so the team patches them first. Which capability is this?
options: Agentic AI, because the model took autonomous action against the appliances, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
Predictive analysis, using models to forecast likely attacks so defenses move before events occur
An AI-augmented baseline, because the VPN traffic pattern deviated from normal, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
A chatbot interaction, because the forecast was delivered in natural language, following the standard change process used across the organization
explain: Forecasting where attacks are likely and acting ahead of them is predictive analysis. No autonomous action, behavioral deviation, or chatbot function is involved.

q: A team is defining guardrails for an AI agent that assists incident response. Which option is the COMPLETE correct guardrail set?
options: Define actions the agent may take alone and forbidden actions, and review the agent's activity during the annual audit, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
Give the agent administrator rights so it can act quickly, and log every action it takes for later review, following the standard change process used across the organization
Define actions the agent may take alone, actions requiring human approval, and forbidden actions; enforce least privilege for the agent and log every action it takes
Define actions requiring human approval and log every action, but let the agent choose its own permission level per incident, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
explain: Guardrails need all three action tiers plus least privilege and full logging; each distractor drops a tier, grants standing admin rights, or lets the agent set its own privileges.

q: A CI/CD pipeline scans every commit and a build fails its security checks. What should the pipeline do?
options: Deploy the build and open a ticket so the findings can be fixed in the next sprint, following the standard change process used across the organization
Disable the scanning stage temporarily so the release schedule is not affected, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
Deploy to production but flag the release as untrusted in the change record, under the direction of the accountable system owner
Block the failing build from deploying while allowing the pipeline to report the findings to the developers
explain: The pipeline's security value is the gate: a failing build does not deploy. Deploying with a ticket or disabling the scan converts the control into documentation.

q: An employee reports a suspicious email that reached 300 mailboxes. Which automated FIRST step gives the response its speed advantage?
options: The workflow searches for and pulls the message from every mailbox it reached, a volume no analyst could finish manually in time
The workflow emails all 300 recipients asking them to delete the message and confirm by reply, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
The workflow forwards the message to the security team's shared mailbox for review the next business day, under the direction of the accountable system owner
The workflow changes every recipient's password as a precaution before analysis begins, using only the tools already approved for this environment
explain: Automation's value is doing the high-volume search-and-remediate step at machine speed across all mailboxes. Asking users to self-delete is slow and unreliable, and password resets precede any evidence.

q: In the phishing playbook, a sandbox detonation scores an attachment as highly malicious, and an agent isolates the one workstation that opened it without waiting for approval. Why is no human gate required here?
options: Agents never require approval for any action taken during a declared incident, under the direction of the accountable system owner
Host isolation is on the pre-approved action list because it is scoped, reversible, and time-critical
The sandbox score legally transfers decision authority from the analyst to the agent, using only the tools already approved for this environment
Isolation is considered a chatbot function, and chatbots are exempt from approval gates, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
explain: Pre-approved lists exist for actions that are bounded and reversible, so the agent can act at machine speed. Broad or irreversible actions still wait for a human.

q: A workflow enriches every incoming ticket with asset owner, device posture, and related alerts before an analyst sees it. What is the PRIMARY benefit?
options: Tickets can be closed automatically without analyst involvement in most cases, using only the tools already approved for this environment
The enrichment removes the need for an asset inventory in the CMDB, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
Analysts start with context already gathered, so judgment is spent on decisions instead of manual data collection
Enrichment guarantees that the ticket's severity rating is always correct, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
explain: Enrichment and routing automate the gathering, not the judgment. It does not close tickets by itself, replace the inventory it draws from, or guarantee correct severity.

q: Before a new automated response playbook goes live, what should the team do FIRST?
options: Enable it for the entire environment so its effectiveness can be measured quickly, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
Remove its logging so test actions do not clutter the production ticket queue, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
Give the playbook permanent credentials with the broadest available permissions, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
Test it in a limited scope against representative cases so a logic error cannot act across the whole environment at once
explain: Scoped testing contains the blast radius of a wrong automation before it runs at machine speed everywhere. Broad enablement and broad credentials maximize the damage a defect can do.

q: An AI agent's service account is found to hold permissions to modify identity policies, though it only needs to read alerts and isolate hosts. Which principle was violated?
options: Least privilege for the agent itself; automation identities must hold only the rights their defined actions require
Separation of duties, because the agent both reads alerts and isolates hosts, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
Defense in depth, because the agent operates at only one control layer, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
Zero trust, because the agent runs inside the corporate network boundary, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
explain: Guardrails apply to the agent's own identity: excess permissions let a misbehaving or manipulated agent do forbidden damage. Reading alerts and isolating hosts are compatible duties, not a separation conflict.

q: A chatbot summarizing tickets begins inventing ticket details that were never in the source records. What is the BEST operational response?
options: Let analysts keep using the summaries, since occasional invented details are normal for chatbots, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
Treat the output as a draft requiring analyst verification, restrict the chatbot to source-grounded summaries, and log the failures
Have the chatbot approve its own summaries with a second automated pass before delivery, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
Replace analyst review with chatbot summaries entirely to remove human inconsistency, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
explain: Chatbot output is first-pass assistance, not evidence; invented details mean outputs must be verified against sources and the tool constrained. Self-approval by the same class of tool does not verify anything.

q: Which division of labor BEST reflects the goal of security automation?
options: Machines handle all steps of routine incidents and humans handle only executive reporting, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
Humans handle detection while machines handle all communication with regulators and customers, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
Machines handle repetitive, high-volume steps; humans spend their judgment on ambiguous, high-impact decisions
Machines and humans each handle half of every task so neither is fully responsible, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
explain: Automation exists to free human judgment for where it matters, not to remove humans from accountability. External communication and final decisions remain human responsibilities.

q: An AI-augmented baseline flags an executive's unusual data access during a genuine acquisition project, generating repeated false alerts. What is the BEST tuning response?
options: Disable baseline alerting for all executive accounts to stop the noise permanently, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
Raise the global alert threshold until executive activity no longer triggers it, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
Switch the system back to fixed thresholds for every user in the organization, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
Feed the confirmed business context back so the baseline learns the new legitimate pattern, and keep the deviation alerting in place
explain: Baselines improve by learning verified legitimate patterns; exempting executives or raising global thresholds blinds the system to real insider misuse, which often hides behind senior accounts.

q: A SOAR playbook that disables user accounts is triggered by a single failed-login threshold and locks out a service team during a password rollout. Which guardrail was missing?
options: A safeguard such as rate limits, exclusion lists for critical accounts, or human approval before mass account disablement
An encryption control to protect the playbook's stored credentials at rest, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
A chatbot to explain to locked-out users why their accounts were disabled, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
A predictive model to forecast the next password rollout date, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
explain: Disabling accounts is high-impact, so the playbook needed containment on its own actions — exclusions, rate limits, or a human gate. Encryption and explanations do not prevent the harmful action.

q: Management asks why the SOC keeps analysts in the loop for an AI agent that has performed well for six months. What is the BEST justification?
options: Analysts must approve actions so their jobs remain necessary as automation expands, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
Guardrails stay because a single bad input or manipulated prompt can make the agent act wrongly at scale, and accountability for irreversible actions must remain human

Regulations prohibit any automated security action without a human clicking approve, following the standard change process used across the organization, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
Six months is too short to evaluate an agent, which needs at least five years of data, under the direction of the accountable system owner, using only the tools already approved for this environment
explain: Human gates exist for impact and accountability, not job protection, and they target irreversible actions rather than every action. Performance history does not remove the failure mode.

q: A team wants an agentic AI to gather evidence from endpoints during investigations. Which design is MOST appropriate?
options: Grant the agent full endpoint control so evidence collection is never blocked by permissions, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
Allow the agent to delete suspicious files during collection to speed up the investigation, following the standard change process used across the organization
Grant the agent read-only evidence-collection rights, require approval for any disruptive action, and log every collection it performs
Let the agent operate without logging so collected evidence stays confidential, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
explain: Evidence gathering is a read-oriented, pre-approvable function; destructive actions need gates, and unlogged collection breaks chain of custody. Full control exceeds the task's needs.

q: Predictive analysis suggests a business unit's servers are the most likely ransomware targets this month. What is the MOST appropriate use of that forecast?
options: Shut the servers down for the month so the predicted attack cannot succeed, following the standard change process used across the organization
Notify law enforcement that an attack on those servers has occurred, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
Reassign the unit's staff to other duties until the forecast period passes, under the direction of the accountable system owner
Prioritize patching, backup verification, and monitoring for those servers ahead of lower-risk systems
explain: Forecasts steer defensive priority — hardening and readiness where risk concentrates. Nothing has occurred yet, so shutdowns and incident notifications are disproportionate.

q: An automated workflow routes critical alerts to the on-call analyst and informational alerts to a daily digest. This is an example of what?
options: Orchestration: coordinating tools and steps so the right work reaches the right place in the right order
Agentic AI, because the workflow makes decisions without human input, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
Predictive analysis, because the workflow forecasts which alerts matter, under the direction of the accountable system owner
A guardrail, because the workflow limits what the alerting tool can do, using only the tools already approved for this environment
explain: Routing and enrichment across tools is orchestration. No autonomous agent, forecast, or action boundary is described.

q: A playbook step that reformats and wipes a workstation runs correctly in testing but is later found to trigger on a broader alert class than intended. What failed?
options: The workstation's disk encryption, which should have prevented the wipe from succeeding, under the direction of the accountable system owner
The playbook's scope definition and testing did not cover the wider trigger, so a destructive step fired outside its intended cases
The ticketing system's enrichment, which added too much context to the alert, using only the tools already approved for this environment
The chatbot summary, which described the alert class incorrectly to analysts, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
explain: Destructive automation lives or dies on trigger scope; an over-broad trigger is a design and testing failure. Encryption does not stop an authorized wipe, and enrichment did not cause the trigger.

q: Which metric BEST shows whether a tier-1 chatbot is helping the SOC?
options: The chatbot answers more questions each week than the analysts do, using only the tools already approved for this environment, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
The chatbot's responses are longer and more detailed than analyst responses, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
Analysts spend less time on routine questions and ticket summaries while the accuracy of chatbot drafts stays verified and high
Fewer tickets are created because users stop reporting minor issues, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
explain: Value is analyst time redirected to judgment work without losing accuracy. Raw volume, verbosity, or suppressed reporting can all rise while the SOC gets worse.

q: A vendor proposes an AI agent that will 'handle incidents end to end with no human involvement.' Which response aligns with sound operations?
options: Accept it, because removing humans removes the largest source of incident errors, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
Accept it only for nights and weekends when analysts are unavailable, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
Deploy it in shadow mode permanently so it can recommend but never be evaluated, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
Reject the unbounded design; define the agent's permitted, approval-gated, and forbidden actions before any deployment
explain: Agentic AI is deployed inside guardrails, not as an unbounded replacement for accountable responders. Shadow mode forever never realizes or tests the capability.

q: In a mature automated response, which action should remain human-approved even though an agent could perform it technically?
options: Blocking a critical vendor's domain across the entire tenant, because a false positive could halt business operations
Pulling a reported phishing email from the mailboxes it reached, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
Opening a case and attaching the indicators from a detonated attachment, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
Isolating a single workstation that executed a confirmed malicious attachment, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
explain: The dividing line is blast radius and reversibility: tenant-wide blocking can cut off a real vendor, while mailbox pulls, case creation, and single-host isolation are scoped and reversible.

q: Why do AI-augmented baselines detect some incidents that fixed thresholds miss?
options: They compare traffic against a larger database of known malware signatures, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
They flag behavior that breaks no numeric rule but does not fit the learned pattern for that user or system
They lower every threshold automatically until at least one alert fires daily, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
They require attackers to authenticate twice before accessing any resource, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
explain: A bulk download under every numeric limit still deviates from a user's pattern, and deviation is what baselines catch. Signature matching and threshold lowering describe other mechanisms.

q: Monitoring flags mass file changes on a file server at 07:12, and the on-call analyst confirms ransomware behavior at 07:20. What is the NEXT phase of the response?
options: Eradication: remove the attacker's tooling from every affected machine, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
Recovery: restore the file server from the most recent clean backup, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
Containment: isolate the server and fence the affected segment to stop the spread before any rebuilding begins
Lessons learned: schedule the post-incident review with leadership, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
explain: Detection and analysis are done; containment comes before eradication and recovery, and restoring an uncontained server invites reinfection. Lessons learned close the process.

q: During a ransomware incident, a manager demands the file server be restored immediately to meet a deadline, before the team has isolated it. What should the incident commander do?
options: Restore the server but monitor it closely so any new encryption is caught quickly, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
Restore a copy of the server to a new segment while leaving the original online, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
Skip containment only if the deadline is documented in the incident ticket, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
Hold the sequence: containment first, because restoring into an active spread risks losing the restored data and widening the incident
explain: Containment is the step nobody may skip; an unrestored-but-contained incident is recoverable, while a rushed restore during active spread compounds the loss.

q: Which activity belongs to the PREPARATION phase of incident response?
options: Writing playbooks, assigning incident roles, and staging tools before any incident occurs
Isolating affected hosts during the first hour of a confirmed incident, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
Interviewing witnesses while the timeline of an incident is reconstructed, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
Restoring services from backup and monitoring them for recurrence, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
explain: Preparation is everything done in advance — plans, playbooks, roles, tools. Isolation is containment, interviews support analysis, and restoration is recovery.

q: Who owns decisions during a major incident, such as whether to take a revenue system offline?
options: The technical lead, because they understand the systems most deeply, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
The incident commander, who holds decision authority while the technical lead runs the hands-on response
The communications lead, because the decision affects customer messaging, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
The scribe, because they hold the most complete record of the incident, following the standard change process used across the organization
explain: Roles are assigned in advance precisely so decisions are not negotiated mid-crisis: the commander decides, the technical lead executes, the scribe records, and communications handles statements.

q: What is the PRIMARY purpose of the scribe role during an incident?
options: To approve all external statements before they are released to customers, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
To direct the technical work of isolating and rebuilding affected systems, following the standard change process used across the organization
To keep the timeline of events and decisions that the post-incident report will be written from
To negotiate with the attacker if the incident involves extortion, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
explain: An accurate contemporaneous timeline is what makes the PIR and any later legal or regulatory account possible. Approvals, technical direction, and negotiation belong to other roles.

q: Customer files were encrypted in an incident, and counsel notes a legal notification deadline. Which activity does this trigger?
options: Eradication of the attacker's tooling from the remaining affected machines, following the standard change process used across the organization
A tabletop exercise to rehearse the notification process with leadership, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
Recovery of the customer file systems from immutable backups, under the direction of the accountable system owner, using only the tools already approved for this environment
Notification and external reporting to regulators and affected customers within the deadlines set by law and contract
explain: Notification duties run on legal clocks that start during the incident, handled with counsel involved from the start. The other options are separate phases or rehearsals.

q: On day two of an incident, the team closes the phished VPN account that let the attacker in and removes attacker tooling from two other machines. Which phase is this?
options: Eradication: removing the attacker's presence and the root cause that admitted them
Containment: stopping the spread of the incident to additional systems, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
Recovery: returning affected services to normal operation, under the direction of the accountable system owner
Detection: identifying that malicious activity is present, using only the tools already approved for this environment
explain: Closing the entry vector and removing tooling eliminates the attacker and the cause — eradication. Containment already happened when systems were isolated.

q: Services are restored from immutable backups on day three and watched closely for signs of the attacker returning. Which phase is this?
options: Eradication
Recovery
Containment
Preparation
explain: Restoring from clean backups and monitoring the restored services is recovery. Eradication — removing the attacker and root cause — must already be complete before restore.

q: Ten days after an incident, a document lands describing the timeline, the decisions made, and committed fixes such as MFA on the VPN and a scheduled restore test. What is this document?
options: The incident playbook for ransomware events
The external notification sent to affected customers
The post-incident report produced during lessons learned
The tabletop exercise scenario for the next quarter
explain: The PIR records what happened, what was decided, and what the organization commits to fix — the output of lessons learned. Playbooks are written before incidents; notifications go to outsiders.

q: A ransomware group demands payment and threatens to publish stolen data. Leadership asks who should communicate with the group. What is the BEST answer?
options: The incident commander should negotiate directly to keep decisions fast, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
The communications lead should negotiate, since the role already handles external statements, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
Any available analyst can negotiate using the group's chat portal, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
Negotiation is a specialist activity handled with legal counsel involved, because it carries legal and sanctions tripwires
explain: Extortion negotiation involves legal exposure, sanctions risk, and evidence duties, so it is done by specialists with counsel — not improvised by incident staff. Communications handles legitimate stakeholders, not attackers.

q: Which statement BEST describes the purpose of a playbook?
options: Per-incident-type instructions that turn the response process into concrete steps responders can follow under pressure
A legal contract defining notification deadlines for each regulator, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
A chronological record of everything that happened during one incident, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
A list of approved vendors who can be engaged during an emergency, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
explain: Playbooks are written in advance, per incident type, so responders execute rather than improvise. The incident record is the timeline/PIR, and deadlines live in legal requirements.

q: A company runs a tabletop exercise for a simulated breach. What is the PRIMARY value?
options: Producing evidence that no incident will occur during the coming year, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
Rehearsing roles, decisions, and communications cheaply before a real incident tests them for real
Testing whether backups can be restored within the recovery time objective, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
Training end users to recognize phishing emails through simulation, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
explain: Tabletops exercise the human system — who decides, who speaks, what the playbooks say — at low cost. Backup restoration is a technical test, and phishing training targets a different audience.

q: An alert fires for impossible-travel logins. An analyst reviews the logs, confirms the account is genuinely compromised, and declares an incident. Which phase did the analyst just complete?
options: Detection
Containment
Analysis
Preparation
explain: The alert itself was detection; evaluating it, confirming true malicious activity, and declaring the incident is analysis. Containment actions follow the declaration.

q: During containment of a worm outbreak, which action is MOST appropriate?
options: Reimaging every workstation in the building, including unaffected departments, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
Restoring the domain controllers from backup to a known-good state, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
Publishing the post-incident report to all staff to raise awareness, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
Segmenting the affected VLAN and disabling the compromised service accounts driving the spread
explain: Containment limits spread with targeted isolation and account disablement. Organization-wide reimaging and restores belong to later phases and waste the containment window.

q: Why must eradication address the root cause and not only remove visible malware?
options: If the entry vector stays open, the attacker or another actor can return through the same path after recovery
Root cause analysis is required to assign blame for the incident report, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
Malware removal tools cannot run until the root cause document is signed, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
Recovery cannot begin until the lessons-learned meeting has been held, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
explain: Eradication means the attacker and their way in are both gone; cleaning machines while the phished, MFA-less VPN stays open invites immediate re-entry. Blame is not the purpose.

q: Legal counsel joins an incident from the start rather than after containment. What is the MAIN reason?
options: Counsel must approve every technical containment action before it is taken, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
Notification duties, evidence handling, and regulatory deadlines may apply from the earliest moments and shape response decisions
Counsel runs the forensic imaging process for affected systems, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
Counsel is responsible for negotiating the incident's internal timeline, following the standard change process used across the organization
explain: Legal rides along early because deadlines and evidence duties start immediately, not because counsel directs technical work or performs forensics.

q: During a ransomware incident, a team restores the affected servers from backup and returns them to production. Within hours the ransomware detonates again, because the original intrusion path was never removed. Which incident response phase did the team skip before recovery?
options: Eradication — the malware, persistence mechanisms, and compromised accounts must be removed before systems are rebuilt and returned to service
Preparation — the team's tools and playbooks must be rewritten and rehearsed with the full response team before any restored system is allowed back onto the production network
Lessons learned — a post-incident review must be completed and signed off before recovery of any affected system can begin
Detection — the original alerts must be re-analyzed and re-triaged before any restored system is reconnected to the network
explain: Recovery before eradication rebuilds on top of the attacker's foothold, so the incident repeats. Eradication removes the malware, persistence mechanisms, and compromised credentials first; preparation happens before incidents, lessons learned come after recovery, and detection already occurred.

q: A business email compromise is discovered after a fraudulent payment was sent. Which containment action comes FIRST?
options: Interview the employee whose mailbox was used, to establish the full timeline, following the standard change process used across the organization
Restore the mailbox from the backup taken the night before the compromise, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
Send a company-wide email warning staff about business email compromise, under the direction of the accountable system owner
Disable or restrict the compromised mailbox and revoke its sessions and rules the attacker created
explain: Containment stops ongoing harm: kill the access and the attacker's inbox rules first. Interviews and warnings support analysis and awareness but do not stop the attacker still inside the mailbox.

q: After recovery, a restored server is placed under heightened monitoring for two weeks. Why?
options: To catch signs the attacker retained access or left persistence that eradication missed, before the incident is closed
Because restored servers cannot be patched during the first two weeks, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
To generate the evidence required for the external notification letter, under the direction of the accountable system owner
Because monitoring tools must be recalibrated after every restore operation, using only the tools already approved for this environment
explain: Recovery includes watching: if persistence survived, monitoring catches the return while responders are still engaged. It is not a patching restriction or a notification artifact.

q: An incident is declared over by the technical team, but no review is scheduled and the same VPN weakness remains unpatched a month later. Which phase was skipped?
options: Analysis, because the team never confirmed the incident was real, under the direction of the accountable system owner
Lessons learned, including the post-incident report and the committed fixes it should have produced
Containment, because the VPN should have been isolated during the incident, using only the tools already approved for this environment
Detection, because monitoring failed to flag the weakness in advance, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
explain: The PIR and lessons learned convert an incident into fixes; without them the root weakness survives to be exploited again. The incident itself was detected, analyzed, and contained.

q: A hospital's incident plan names an incident commander, technical lead, scribe, communications lead, and legal contact in advance. What problem does this solve?
options: It guarantees the hospital will pass its next compliance audit, using only the tools already approved for this environment
It removes the need for playbooks for specific incident types, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
A crisis does not become a negotiation about who decides, who acts, and who speaks
It ensures insurance will cover the cost of any future incident, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
explain: Pre-assigned roles remove decision ambiguity under pressure. They do not replace playbooks or guarantee audit or insurance outcomes.

q: Which event MOST clearly marks the transition from detection to analysis?
options: A monitoring tool generates an alert for an anomalous event, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
A playbook is opened for the corresponding incident type, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
Affected systems are isolated from the production network, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
An analyst evaluates the alert against logs and context and confirms whether malicious activity is actually occurring
explain: Detection produces the signal; analysis is the human evaluation that confirms or dismisses it. Isolation is containment, which follows a confirmed analysis.

q: During a data theft incident, executives want to wipe and rebuild the affected server immediately to 'get clean.' What is the risk of complying before investigators finish?
options: Wiping destroys evidence needed to scope the theft, support notification duties, and prove what was taken
Wiping the server will automatically notify the attacker that they were discovered, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
Rebuilt servers cannot rejoin the domain for 30 days after an incident, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
The wipe will void the organization's cyber insurance in all circumstances, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
explain: Evidence preservation and scoping come before destructive rebuilding; without them the organization cannot know what was taken or meet its reporting duties. The other claims are invented absolutes.

q: A regulator's notification deadline for a breach is 72 hours from awareness. When should the notification work begin?
options: After recovery is complete and all systems are back to normal operation, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
As soon as the incident is confirmed and counsel is engaged, in parallel with containment and eradication
After the post-incident report is finalized and approved by leadership, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
Only if the attacker confirms publicly that data was exfiltrated, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
explain: Legal clocks run from awareness, not from the end of the technical response, so notification preparation runs in parallel. Waiting for recovery or the PIR guarantees a missed deadline.

q: Two departments argue mid-incident about whether to shut down the customer portal. According to sound incident structure, how is this resolved?
options: The department that owns the portal decides, since it is their system, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
The decision waits until the next scheduled leadership meeting, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
The incident commander decides, informed by the technical lead's assessment and the business impact
The communications lead decides based on how the shutdown will look publicly, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
explain: Decision authority is centralized in the commander precisely to avoid mid-incident deadlock. Ownership and optics inform the decision but do not make it.

q: A playbook for a lost-laptop incident is missing, so responders improvise and forget to revoke the device's certificates for two days. Which preparation improvement addresses this?
options: Buy additional monitoring tools so lost laptops are detected faster, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
Require employees to report lost laptops within one hour of discovery, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
Extend the incident response retainer with the external forensics firm, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
Build and maintain per-incident-type playbooks, and rehearse them in tabletop exercises so gaps surface before real incidents
explain: The failure was missing instructions, not missing detection; playbooks plus rehearsal are the preparation fix. Faster reporting helps but does not supply the missing steps.

q: What distinguishes containment from eradication?
options: Containment stops the incident from spreading; eradication removes the attacker and the root cause entirely
Containment removes malware; eradication restores services from backup, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
Containment happens after recovery; eradication happens before detection, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
Containment is performed by management; eradication is performed by legal, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
explain: The phases differ by purpose: limit the blast radius first, then eliminate the presence and its cause, then recover. The distractors swap in recovery or invent ownership rules.

q: An organization suffers the same phishing-led compromise three times in a year, each time contained and cleaned successfully. What does the pattern MOST likely indicate?
options: Detection tooling is too sensitive and is generating duplicate incidents, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
Lessons learned are not converting into durable fixes, so the root weakness survives each response
Containment is being performed too quickly, before analysis finishes, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
The organization needs to renegotiate its incident response retainer, following the standard change process used across the organization
explain: Repeat incidents through the same vector mean the PIR's committed fixes — MFA, filtering, training — were never implemented. The responses themselves worked; the follow-through failed.

q: During an incident, a well-meaning engineer posts detailed technical findings to a public status page. Which role should have prevented this?
options: The scribe, who should have locked the incident documentation, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
The technical lead, who should have revoked the engineer's access, following the standard change process used across the organization
The communications lead, who owns internal and external statements during the incident
Legal counsel, who should have pre-approved the status page design, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
explain: External statements flow through the communications lead so disclosures are accurate, timed, and legally safe. Ad hoc technical posts can tip off attackers and create liability.

q: Which preparation activity MOST improves the first hour of a real incident?
options: Purchasing a larger SIEM license to ingest more log sources, following the standard change process used across the organization
Extending log retention from 90 days to one year across all systems, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
Requiring all staff to complete annual phishing awareness training, under the direction of the accountable system owner
Maintaining tested playbooks and an up-to-date contact and escalation list for the named incident roles
explain: The first hour is consumed by coordination: who to call, what steps to follow. Log volume and retention matter later in the investigation, not in the opening coordination.

q: Investigators arrive at a running workstation suspected of hosting fileless malware. Which evidence should be captured FIRST?
options: A memory dump, because RAM holds running processes, live connections, and decrypted content that vanish at power-off
A bit-level disk image, because the disk is the most complete evidence source, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
Surveillance footage of the workstation area for the past week, under the direction of the accountable system owner, using only the tools already approved for this environment
The user's badge records for the building on the day in question, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
explain: Order of volatility puts memory first: it is the most perishable evidence and the home of fileless malware. Disk, video, and badge records all survive longer.

q: A responder powers off a suspect machine 'to stop the malware' before capturing anything. What was MOST likely lost?
options: The disk image, because powered-off disks cannot be imaged forensically, under the direction of the accountable system owner
Volatile memory contents: running processes, network connections, encryption keys, and fileless payloads
The NetFlow records stored on the network's flow collectors, using only the tools already approved for this environment
The surveillance footage recorded by the building's camera system, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
explain: Power-off destroys RAM and everything only it held. Disks can still be imaged afterward, and flow records and footage live on other systems.

q: To scope an intrusion quickly, an analyst needs to know which hosts a compromised server contacted over the past month and how much data moved. Which source is BEST?
options: Full packet captures from the server's network segment for the entire month, using only the tools already approved for this environment
A memory dump taken from the compromised server today, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
NetFlow/IPFIX records, which compactly log who talked to whom, when, and how much, and are retained for months
The server's local firewall log, which rotates every 24 hours, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
explain: Flow records are built for scoping: compact, long-retained connection metadata. A month of full captures is rarely retained, and today's memory and a daily-rotating log cannot cover the period.

q: When does full packet capture matter MORE than flow records?
options: When the investigation covers a retention window longer than a few days, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
When the analyst needs to identify which hosts communicated at all, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
When the evidence must be collected before a memory dump is taken, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
When the investigation needs the actual content of communications, not just endpoints, timing, and volume
explain: Flows answer who, when, and how much; only packet capture shows what was said. For long windows and host discovery, compact flow data is the practical source.

q: A forensic examiner is imaging a suspect laptop's drive. Which option is the COMPLETE correct procedure?
options: Photograph and note the machine's state, capture memory first, image the disk bit-by-bit through a write blocker, hash the image with SHA-256, log it in the custody record, and analyze only the copy

Image the disk bit-by-bit through a write blocker, hash the image, and analyze the original drive to save time, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location

Capture memory first, copy the user's documents folder to a USB drive, and hash the copies for the custody record, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review

Photograph the machine, image the disk through a write blocker, and begin analysis on the original while the copy verifies, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
explain: Each step protects the next: volatility order, write blocking, hashing, custody logging, and analyzing copies only. Working on the original or copying selected files breaks forensic soundness.

q: Why is a disk image hashed immediately after acquisition?
options: To encrypt the image so unauthorized staff cannot view its contents, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
So every later copy can be verified against the original hash, proving the evidence has not changed since capture
To compress the image so it fits on the evidence storage system, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
To convert the image into a format that analysis tools can open, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
explain: A hash is a fingerprint, not encryption or compression: matching hashes prove bit-for-bit integrity across every copy and handoff.

q: What is the purpose of a write blocker during disk imaging?
options: It speeds up the imaging process by bypassing the drive's error checking, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
It encrypts the image as it is written to the evidence storage device, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
It prevents the imaging process from altering the original drive, so the evidence source stays exactly as it was found
It blocks the suspect drive from connecting to any network during imaging, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
explain: Even mounting a drive can change timestamps and metadata; the write blocker guarantees the original is only read. Speed, encryption, and networking are not its function.

q: An investigation's key log evidence is challenged because nobody can show who handled the exported files or when. Which practice failed?
options: Order of volatility: the logs should have been collected before memory, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
Log parsing: the exports were not queried with the correct filters, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
Data retention: the logs were kept beyond their scheduled period, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
Chain of custody: the documented, unbroken record of evidence collection, handling, and transfer
explain: Evidence that cannot prove where it has been cannot prove anything else; undocumented handling is a custody failure regardless of how well the logs were analyzed.

q: Analysts suspect a server was compromised sometime in a two-week window but do not know which accounts were used. Which artifact should they query FIRST to build the timeline?
options: System and authentication logs, parsed and filtered across the window for logons, privilege use, and process events
A fresh memory dump of the server taken today, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
Surveillance footage of the server room for the full two weeks, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
The server's hardware warranty and maintenance records, following the standard change process used across the organization
explain: Logs are the timeline source for system activity, and skilled log parsing across the window reconstructs account use. Today's memory cannot show two-week-old events.

q: A virtual machine involved in an incident must be preserved exactly as it is for later analysis while the service moves to a clean instance. Which artifact accomplishes this?
options: A NetFlow export covering the machine's network connections
A snapshot that freezes the machine's current state for analysis
A memory dump uploaded to the ticketing system
A screenshot of the machine's desktop taken by the administrator
explain: A snapshot preserves the VM's full state — disk and configuration — as a point-in-time artifact. Screenshots and flow exports capture fragments, not the machine.

q: Badge records show an employee's card entered the data center at 02:40, but the employee claims to have been home. Which additional source BEST corroborates or refutes the claim?
options: The employee's email out-of-office settings for that week, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
The data center's temperature and humidity sensor logs, following the standard change process used across the organization
Surveillance footage of the data center entrance at that time, which can show who actually used the badge
A memory dump from the server the badge holder is accused of touching, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
explain: Badges prove a card was used, not who held it; camera footage is the physical-world source that ties a person to the event. Sensor logs and server memory cannot identify the badge user.

q: An investigation into a fraudulent wire transfer needs to establish who approved the vendor change and what the approver knew. Which source is MOST relevant?
options: A bit-level image of the finance department's file server, following the standard change process used across the organization, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
NetFlow records between the finance workstation and the bank, under the direction of the accountable system owner, using only the tools already approved for this environment
A memory dump of the approver's workstation taken today, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
Stakeholder records and interviews — HR, legal, and the account owners — whose documentation and testimony complete the timeline
explain: Technical artifacts show system events, but approval and knowledge live with people and their records. Stakeholders are a named evidence source precisely for this layer of the timeline.

q: An analyst must determine whether data left the network during an incident last night. Which option is the COMPLETE correct evidence set to examine together?
options: NetFlow records for volume and destinations, full packet captures where content must be confirmed, and proxy or firewall logs correlating the sessions to users and devices

NetFlow records for the affected segment, reviewed on their own without other sources, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes, under the direction of the accountable system owner

Full packet captures from last night and the endpoint's current memory dump, using only the tools already approved for this environment, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review

Proxy logs correlating sessions to users, plus badge records for the network operations center, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
explain: Exfiltration questions need metadata, content, and identity correlation together; each distractor relies on a single source or adds an irrelevant one, leaving the conclusion unsupported.

q: Why are bit-level copies required for forensic disk images instead of ordinary file copies?
options: A bit-level copy completes faster than copying individual files from the drive, under the direction of the accountable system owner
A bit-level copy captures everything, including deleted files, slack space, and metadata that a file copy leaves behind
A bit-level copy automatically encrypts the evidence during acquisition, using only the tools already approved for this environment
A file copy cannot be hashed, so only bit-level images can be verified, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
explain: Forensic soundness requires the complete physical picture — deleted content and slack space often hold the evidence. File copies also miss the structures that prove how files were handled.

q: During evidence collection, the order of volatility places which item as MORE perishable than a disk image?
options: Archived log exports stored on the evidence server, using only the tools already approved for this environment
Surveillance footage retained by the facilities system, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
Live network connections and running process state held in memory
Badge access records held by physical security, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
explain: Volatility ranks by how fast evidence disappears: live state dies with the process or power, while stored logs, footage, and badge records persist. Memory and its contents are captured before disk work.

q: An analyst needs to prove a specific file existed on a suspect drive with specific content at acquisition time. Which combination provides this?
options: A screenshot of the file's icon in the drive's folder listing, with findings reported to management at the next scheduled review
A printed directory listing signed by the responding analyst, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
The file copied to a USB drive and stored in the evidence locker, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
The bit-level image plus its acquisition SHA-256 hash recorded in the custody log
explain: The image preserves the file in context and the recorded hash proves the image — and therefore the file — is unchanged since capture. Screenshots, listings, and loose copies prove neither content nor integrity.

q: Log timestamps from three systems disagree by several minutes, confusing the incident timeline. What is the underlying lesson?
options: Reliable time synchronization across systems is essential, because investigations correlate events by timestamp across many sources
Logs from different vendors can never be correlated and should be analyzed in isolation, in line with the organization's stated retention requirements
Analysts should convert all timestamps to the time zone of the headquarters office, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
Memory dumps should replace logs as the primary timeline source in every investigation, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
explain: Cross-source correlation is how timelines are built, and clock skew breaks it; synchronized time is an investigative prerequisite. Isolation and time-zone conversion do not fix skew.

q: Which source BEST answers the question 'how much data did the compromised host send to the external address?'
options: The host's current memory dump, reviewed for active connections, whenever the associated account or system is used, from any location
NetFlow/IPFIX records for that host and destination, which quantify bytes per flow over time
The external address's WHOIS registration record, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved
A disk image of the host taken after the incident closed, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
explain: Flow records exist to quantify conversations — endpoints, timing, and byte counts. Memory shows only the present moment, and WHOIS and disk images do not measure transfers.

q: A workstation will be collected as evidence. Which option lists the COMPLETE correct collection order and handling?
options: Image the disk through a write blocker, capture memory afterward, photograph the machine, and hash the image, as part of the normal operating procedure for the team involved, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review

Photograph the machine, image the disk, hash the image, and capture memory if the machine is still running afterward, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
Photograph and document the machine's state, capture memory, collect live network state, image the disk through a write blocker, hash and log everything into the custody record
Capture memory, photograph the machine afterward, copy the disk's files to evidence storage, and hash the copies, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
explain: Volatility order plus documentation and custody at every step is the complete method; imaging before memory loses RAM, and file copies are not forensic images.

q: An analyst reviewing authentication logs notices the attacker used a valid account at unusual hours for two weeks before the visible attack. What does this MOST likely indicate?
options: The account's password expired and the log entries are timestamp errors, and verified during the next periodic access or configuration review
The logs were tampered with, because valid accounts cannot be abused, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
The user was working flexible hours and the entries are unrelated, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
The compromise began earlier than the visible attack, and the investigation's scope and timeline must expand backward
explain: Valid-account misuse at odd hours is a classic early-compromise indicator; investigators widen the window rather than dismiss the evidence. Valid credentials are abused constantly — that is why they are stolen.

q: Why do investigators analyze a copy of a disk image rather than the original image?
options: To preserve the verified original untouched, so analysis actions can never alter the evidence of record
Because analysis tools cannot open an original forensic image format, applied consistently to all in-scope systems and accounts
Because the original image must be returned to the suspect within 24 hours, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
To allow multiple analysts to change the same image simultaneously, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
explain: Analysis is invasive — tools mount, index, and carve — so it happens on working copies while the hashed original stays pristine for verification and court.

q: A cloud workload suspected in an incident exists only as a running instance with no attached persistent disk history. Which artifact BEST preserves its state?
options: A screenshot of the cloud console showing the instance's status page, in accordance with the approved policy for the environment
A snapshot of the instance together with a memory capture, taken before the instance is terminated
An export of the billing records for the instance's running period, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
A copy of the instance's public IP address and DNS name, following the standard change process used across the organization
explain: Ephemeral workloads vanish on termination, so snapshot plus memory preserves the analyzable state. Console screenshots and billing records document existence, not content.

q: HR provides the termination date and access requests for a suspect employee, while legal advises on what may be searched. This illustrates which investigation principle?
options: Technical artifacts alone are sufficient, and stakeholder input is a formality, with the results reviewed by the security team on a regular schedule
Investigations should be run by HR with technical staff in a supporting role only, following the standard change process used across the organization
Stakeholders such as HR and legal are evidence sources and partners whose records and guidance shape a lawful, complete investigation
Legal involvement means the investigation's findings cannot be used internally, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
explain: People and their records complete timelines that systems cannot — employment dates, approvals, and authority to search. Stakeholder involvement complements technical evidence rather than replacing it.

q: An analyst wants to find every system a malicious file touched. The file's hash is known. Which approach is MOST effective?
options: Interview the user who first reported the file and rely on their recollection, following the standard change process used across the organization
Review surveillance footage of the room where the file was first seen, and documented in the central system of record for audit purposes
Check the file's digital signature against the vendor's published list, under the direction of the accountable system owner
